meta.updated: 2026-08-27: xg_for/xg_against for multi-season stints replaced with per-season xg_seasons arrays, recency-weighted at call time by features.manager_prior() using the same MANAGER_PRIOR_HALFLIFE_YEARS=4.0 already used to weight whole stints against each other. Rationale: a flat mean treated a manager's oldest and newest seasons at one club identically, which understates a manager whose style trended up or down (e.g. Rose's Leipzig defence, Moyes's West Ham record, both worsened in their final season there). ppg stays a flat aggregate over the whole stint deliberately -- it answers 'how successful were they overall' (a sample-size question), while xG answers 'what do they look like now' (a recency question); the two numbers are allowed to use different logic because they're doing different jobs. Single-season stints are unaffected (nothing to weight).
meta.method: ppg computed manually from real W/D/L records found via web search (Wikipedia, Premier League official, Bundesliga.com, club sites, verified news outlets). xg_seasons sourced 2026-08 from user-supplied per-season xG tables (manager_xg_data.md); the per-match GF/GA columns in that file were cross-checked against data/raw/matches_football_data.csv (every checkable EPL row matched exactly), which is why the xG figures riding alongside them are trusted. features.manager_prior() defaults still-missing xg_for/xg_against to config.LEAGUE_AVG_XG (neutral, no fabricated shape signal) -- true for any stint below with no xG data at all.
meta.rule: every ppg below is 3*W + D, divided by matches, from a specific sourced W-D-L line -- never taken as a pre-computed PPG from an AI summary (two independent chatbot passes gave self-contradicting PPG for the same stints, see project memory).
meta.gaps: any manager not listed here has no defensible stint data yet; manager_prior() returns None for them and the model widens uncertainty instead of guessing.

St. Pauli.note: 35W 11D 8L, Dec 2022-Jun 2024 (2. Bundesliga). Not cross-checkable -- 2. Bundesliga, outside matches_football_data.csv's EPL-only coverage

Bayer Leverkusen.note: 88W 33D 19L, Oct 2022-2025. 2023-24 was Leverkusen's invincible season, an outlier recency-weighting does not fully correct for either. All-competitions figure (league+cup+UCL), kept deliberately over a Bundesliga-only 93-match/2.161ppg split that was tried and reverted 2026-09-01 -- the league-only version raised ppg slightly but cut effective_matches enough to drop confidence 0.49->0.32 and shrink Chelsea's manager bonus, and the user chose to keep the fuller-volume figure instead. A real Real Madrid stint exists too (19 LaLiga matches, 73.7% win rate) but stays excluded -- genuinely small sample, not a data error.

His final season there was also his worst defensively, so recency-weighting this now reads a somewhat weaker prior than a flat mean did
